name: Groupe SEB
desc: French maker of small kitchen and home appliances and cookware under Tefal, Krups, Rowenta, Moulinex, WMF and Supor brands.
markets: Sells in about 150 countries across Europe, China (Supor), the Americas and Asia-Pacific through retailers and professional channels.
rationale: Household-name appliance brands sold worldwide; F1 offers global consumer reach and a showcase for premium WMF and Krups coffee lines.

name: Reddit
desc: Online platform of user-run topic communities that earns revenue from advertising and from licensing its data for AI training.
markets: US is the core advertising market; large user bases in the UK, Canada, Australia, India and Europe, with international ad sales growing.
rationale: Young, internet-native audience overlaps strongly with F1's growing fan base; ad-funded platform could use partnership for brand campaigns.
parent: Listed on the NYSE in March 2024

name: Central Retail Corporation
desc: Thai retail group running department stores, supermarkets, home improvement, electronics and sports stores, plus online shopping.
markets: Main markets Thailand and Vietnam, plus department stores in Italy (Rinascente); customers are mass-market and middle-class shoppers.
rationale: Large Thai and Vietnamese consumer retailer with sports retail formats; F1 fit mainly regional, around Asian race hospitality and promotions.

name: Laopu Gold
desc: Chinese luxury gold jewellery brand selling handcrafted pieces in traditional styles through its own high-end stores.
markets: Stores in major mainland Chinese cities, Hong Kong and Macau, with a first overseas store opened in Singapore in 2025.
rationale: Fast-growing luxury brand with affluent Chinese clientele; F1 Shanghai and Asian races could build prestige, though international awareness is low.
parent: Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in June 2024

name: NerdWallet
desc: Personal finance website and app comparing credit cards, loans, mortgages, insurance and savings, paid by financial providers for referrals.
markets: Mainly US consumers, with smaller operations in the United Kingdom and Canada.
rationale: Heavy US consumer advertiser; F1's growing US audience fits, though spend is focused on performance marketing rather than sponsorship.
parent: Listed on Nasdaq in 2021

name: Meituan
desc: Chinese local services platform for food delivery, instant retail, restaurant reviews, hotel and travel booking and in-store services.
markets: Mainly China; Keeta food delivery operates in Hong Kong, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, and has launched in Brazil.
rationale: Expanding Keeta brand in the Gulf and Brazil, both F1 host markets; races there could support consumer brand building abroad.

name: Amplifon
desc: Hearing care retailer running audiology clinics that test hearing and fit hearing aids, under Amplifon and Miracle-Ear brands.
markets: Around 10,000 points of sale in roughly 26 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Consumer healthcare brand targeting older affluent customers; F1's broad European and US TV audience offers awareness, though fit is moderate.

name: PayPal
desc: Digital payments company offering the PayPal wallet, Venmo, Braintree merchant processing, Xoom transfers and consumer credit.
markets: Consumers and merchants in about 200 markets; largest business in the US, with major operations in Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global payments brand competing with F1 sponsors such as Visa, Mastercard and American Express; strong consumer and merchant marketing fit.
parent: Separated from eBay in 2015

name: Klarna
desc: Swedish fintech and bank offering buy now pay later, instalment credit, cards, a shopping app and merchant payment tools.
markets: Shoppers and merchants across Europe, the US, the UK and Australia, with the US its main growth market.
rationale: Consumer brand with heavy marketing and US growth focus; rivals Visa, Mastercard and American Express already sponsor F1.
parent: Listed on the NYSE in September 2025

name: FINN
desc: Online car subscription provider offering new cars with insurance, registration and maintenance included in one monthly fee.
markets: Customers in Germany and the United States; no other verified markets.
rationale: Car-focused consumer brand in Germany and the US; F1 links to automotive enthusiasm, though scale and budget are limited.

name: Kavak
desc: Online platform for buying, selling and financing inspected used cars, with warranty, delivery and vehicle management services.
markets: Mexico is the core market; has operated in other Latin American countries and the Gulf, but its current footprint outside Mexico is not confirmed.
rationale: Car-focused consumer brand in Mexico, an F1 host country with a strong fan base; Mexico City Grand Prix offers a natural platform.

name: Faire
desc: Online wholesale marketplace connecting independent retailers with brands, offering ordering, payment terms and shipping.
markets: Retailers and brands in the US, Canada, the UK, Europe and Australia.
rationale: B2B marketplace serving small shop owners, not mass consumers; limited F1 fit beyond niche hospitality.

name: PetSmart
desc: Pet specialty retailer selling pet food and supplies and offering grooming, training, boarding and in-store veterinary clinics.
markets: About 1,650 stores in the United States, Canada and Puerto Rico, plus online sales; no verified expansion beyond North America.
rationale: Mass-market US consumer brand; F1's growing US audience offers reach, but domestic focus and category make fit modest.
parent: BC Partners

name: Carro
desc: Online used-car marketplace combining car sales, financing, insurance, after-sales services and dealer auctions.
markets: Operates in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and other Asian markets.
rationale: Car-focused consumer brand in Singapore and South-East Asia; Singapore Grand Prix gives an obvious local platform.

name: QVC
desc: Video and online retailer selling beauty, fashion, jewellery, home and electronics products through television shopping channels and apps.
markets: Broadcasts in the US, UK, Germany, Italy and Japan (through a joint venture), reaching over 350 million households.
rationale: Retailer with an older, mostly female audience in decline; weak overlap with F1 and limited sponsorship budget.
parent: QVC Group
changed: Parent Qurate Retail renamed QVC Group in 2025

name: Ocado Group
desc: British grocery technology company licensing robotic warehouse and online fulfilment systems to grocers, and co-owning Ocado Retail.
markets: Technology partners include Kroger (US), Sobeys (Canada), Coles (Australia), Aeon (Japan) and others; Ocado Retail serves UK shoppers.
rationale: Robotics and automation story suits a technology showcase; UK consumer brand awareness, though B2B partners are its main customers.

name: Diebold Nixdorf
desc: Supplier of ATMs, self-checkout and point-of-sale systems, software and maintenance services to banks and retailers.
markets: Bank and retail customers in more than 100 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B equipment supplier selling to banks and retailers; F1 hospitality could aid client relations, but consumer brand value is low.
parent: Restructured through Chapter 11 in 2023 and relisted

name: Vinted
desc: Online marketplace where individuals buy and sell second-hand clothing and accessories, with its own shipping network.
markets: Members across about 20 European markets, including France, Germany, the UK, Italy and Spain.
rationale: Large European consumer brand with heavy advertising; F1's young European audience suits, though a sustainability message may clash.

name: FEMSA
desc: Mexican group owning OXXO convenience stores, pharmacies and fuel stations and a large stake in bottler Coca-Cola FEMSA.
markets: Mainly Mexico and Latin America (Colombia, Chile, Peru, Brazil), plus Europe through Valora convenience stores.
rationale: Huge consumer reach through OXXO in Mexico, an F1 host country; Mexico City Grand Prix offers strong activation potential.
parent: Sold most of its Heineken stake in 2023-2024

name: Autodoc
desc: Online retailer of car spare parts and accessories selling to drivers and small workshops through web shops and an app.
markets: Customers in 27 European countries; no verified operations outside Europe.
rationale: Automotive e-commerce brand with motorsport-minded customers across Europe; F1 fits its audience directly.
changed: Planned stock market listing postponed in 2023 and 2025

name: Seven & i Holdings
desc: Japanese retail holding company owning 7-Eleven convenience stores in Japan and North America and licensing the brand worldwide.
markets: 7-Eleven stores across Japan, the US and Canada, with licensees in Asia, Europe and Australia.
rationale: Globally known convenience brand; F1 offers reach in Japan and the US, though marketing is mostly local.
parent: Rejected Couche-Tard takeover approach, withdrawn in 2025; sold control of superstore unit York Holdings in 2025

name: Flix (FlixBus)
desc: Intercity bus and train operator selling FlixBus, FlixTrain and Greyhound tickets, with partner companies running most buses.
markets: Bus services in about 45 countries in Europe, North America, South America and Asia; owns Greyhound in the US.
rationale: Mass-market travel brand across Europe and the US; F1 offers youth reach, though travel promotions are more likely than headline sponsorship.

name: Carsome
desc: Online used-car platform that inspects, buys and sells cars to consumers and dealers, with financing and insurance.
markets: Operates in Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore; no verified plans beyond South-East Asia.
rationale: Car-focused consumer brand in South-East Asia; Singapore Grand Prix and regional F1 interest give a moderate fit.

name: Vestiaire Collective
desc: Online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned luxury and designer fashion, with item authentication.
markets: Buyers and sellers in about 80 countries, mainly Europe and the US, with offices in Paris, London and New York.
rationale: Luxury resale brand targeting affluent fashion buyers; F1 paddock audience fits, though budget is limited.

name: Sally Beauty Holdings
desc: Specialty retailer and distributor of professional hair colour, hair care and nail products to consumers and salons.
markets: About 4,000 stores in the US, Canada, Mexico, the UK, Ireland, Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, Chile and Peru.
rationale: Beauty supply retailer with mostly female, salon-focused customers and little sports marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Cencosud
desc: Chilean retailer running supermarkets, department stores, home improvement stores, shopping centres and consumer finance.
markets: Stores in Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Peru, Colombia and Uruguay, plus The Fresh Market in the United States.
rationale: Major Latin American consumer brand; F1 races in Brazil and Mexico could support regional activation, but fit is moderate.

name: QVC Group
desc: US group operating QVC and HSN television and online shopping networks and Cornerstone home brands such as Frontgate.
markets: Mainly the US; QVC also broadcasts in the UK, Germany, Italy and Japan through a joint venture.
rationale: Declining TV retail group with an older, mostly female audience; weak F1 fit.
parent: Renamed QVC Group from Qurate Retail in 2025; sold Zulily in 2023

name: PDD Holdings
desc: Owner of Pinduoduo, a Chinese discount e-commerce marketplace, and Temu, an international low-price online shopping platform.
markets: Pinduoduo serves China; Temu sells in the US, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Temu is a heavy global advertiser seeking mass reach; F1 offers worldwide audience, though regulatory scrutiny may deter.

name: eBay
desc: Online marketplace where consumers and businesses buy and sell new and used goods through auctions and fixed-price listings.
markets: Marketplaces in about 190 markets; largest in the US, UK, Germany and Australia.
rationale: Global consumer marketplace with a large car parts and collectibles business; F1 fans overlap with motors and collectibles buyers.

name: Fnac Darty
desc: French retailer selling consumer electronics, household appliances, books, music and tickets through stores, franchises and online.
markets: France, Belgium, Spain, Portugal and Switzerland, plus Italy through the Unieuro acquisition.
rationale: European mass-market retailer focused on France; F1 offers limited added value beyond domestic promotions.
parent: Formed when Fnac acquired Darty in 2016

name: H&M Group
desc: Swedish fashion retailer selling clothing, accessories and homeware under H&M, COS, Weekday, Monki, & Other Stories and Arket.
markets: Thousands of stores in about 75 markets across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East, plus online.
rationale: Global youth fashion brand; F1's young and growing female fan base suits merchandise collaborations, as rivals in fashion already partner teams.

name: Shopify
desc: Canadian e-commerce software company providing online store, point-of-sale, payments and checkout tools to merchants of all sizes.
markets: Millions of merchants worldwide; the US is the largest market, with growth in Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Commerce platform courting large enterprise merchants; F1 offers a technology showcase and B2B hospitality alongside rival tech sponsors.

name: Signet Jewelers
desc: Diamond jewellery retailer operating Kay, Zales, Jared, Banter, Blue Nile, H.Samuel and Ernest Jones stores and websites.
markets: Mainly the United States, plus Canada and the United Kingdom.
rationale: Mid-market jewellery retailer focused on US consumers; F1's growing US audience offers some reach but fit is limited.

name: Zalando
desc: Online fashion and beauty retailer selling clothing, shoes and cosmetics from thousands of brands, plus logistics services for brands.
markets: About 62 million active customers in around 30 European markets; acquired About You in 2025.
rationale: Leading European fashion e-commerce brand; F1's young European audience suits lifestyle and merchandise campaigns.
parent: Acquired About You in 2025

name: American Eagle Outfitters
desc: Apparel retailer selling jeans, casual clothing and intimates under American Eagle and Aerie brands through stores and online.
markets: Stores in the US, Canada and Mexico, with licensed partner stores in some other countries.
rationale: Youth apparel brand in North America; F1's growing young US audience offers some fit for collaborations.

name: Copart
desc: Online vehicle auction company selling salvage and used cars for insurers, dealers and fleets through physical yards.
markets: Operates in 11 countries: the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, Ireland, Brazil, Spain, UAE, Bahrain, Oman and Finland.
rationale: B2B vehicle remarketing business with limited consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond automotive association.

name: Global-e
desc: Cross-border e-commerce platform that handles local pricing, duties, payments, shipping and returns for online merchants.
markets: Merchants in the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific selling to shoppers in over 200 markets; Shopify is a key partner.
rationale: B2B platform invisible to shoppers; F1 could serve client hospitality with fashion and luxury merchants, but fit is modest.
parent: Listed on Nasdaq in 2021

name: Shoprite Holdings
desc: African food retailer running Shoprite, Checkers, Usave and other supermarkets, plus liquor, pharmacy and furniture stores.
markets: Mainly South Africa, plus several neighbouring Southern African countries; it has exited most markets elsewhere in Africa.
rationale: Mass-market grocer in South Africa with no current F1 race; weak fit.

name: Abbott Laboratories
desc: US healthcare company making medical devices, diagnostic tests, nutrition products such as Similac and Ensure, and branded generic drugs.
markets: Sells in over 160 countries; non-US sales include branded generic medicines in emerging markets.
rationale: Global consumer health and device brand, including FreeStyle Libre for active people; health-tech showcase possible, but fit is moderate.

name: AstraZeneca
desc: Anglo-Swedish drug maker developing and selling medicines for cancer, cardiovascular, respiratory, immune and rare diseases.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US, Europe, China and emerging markets as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: Bayer
desc: German life sciences group selling prescription drugs, crop protection and seeds, and consumer health products such as Aspirin.
markets: Sells worldwide to farmers, health systems and consumers across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Well-known consumer health and agriculture brand with a sports sponsorship tradition; F1 hospitality and global reach possible, fit moderate.
parent: Acquired Monsanto in 2018

name: Bristol Myers Squibb
desc: US drug maker selling medicines for blood clots, cancer, immune disorders and blood cancers, including Eliquis and Opdivo.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Acquired Celgene in 2019

name: Sanofi
desc: French drug maker selling immunology medicines such as Dupixent, vaccines, rare-disease and other prescription medicines.
markets: Sells in around 170 countries, with the US and Europe as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Sold control of consumer health unit Opella to CD&R in 2025

name: Thermo Fisher Scientific
desc: Supplier of laboratory instruments, reagents, consumables, diagnostics and clinical research services to pharma, hospitals and research labs.
markets: Customers in pharma, biotech, healthcare, academia and industry across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B science supplier with little consumer brand; F1 could serve client hospitality and a precision-engineering message, but fit is modest.

name: Danaher
desc: US group owning life sciences and diagnostics businesses such as Cytiva, Beckman Coulter, Leica Microsystems, SCIEX and Cepheid.
markets: Sells to labs, pharma and hospitals worldwide across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B science conglomerate with low brand visibility; limited F1 fit beyond client hospitality.
parent: Spun off Veralto in 2023

name: Gilead Sciences
desc: US biopharmaceutical company selling medicines for HIV, hepatitis B and C, COVID-19 and cancer, including Biktarvy.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: GSK
desc: British drug and vaccine maker selling vaccines such as Shingrix, HIV medicines through ViiV Healthcare, and specialty medicines.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US and Europe as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Renamed GSK plc from GlaxoSmithKline in 2022; demerged Haleon in 2022

name: IQVIA
desc: Provider of clinical trial services, healthcare data, analytics and commercial outsourcing to pharma, biotech and medical device companies.
markets: Clients in over 100 countries across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B data and research brand; F1 data analytics tie-in conceivable, but low brand value with consumers.
parent: Formed by 2016 merger of Quintiles and IMS Health

name: Novartis
desc: Swiss drug maker developing and selling innovative prescription medicines for heart, immune, cancer and neurological diseases.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US, Europe and China as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Spun off Sandoz in 2023

name: Sandoz Group
desc: Swiss maker of generic and biosimilar medicines sold to pharmacies, hospitals and health systems.
markets: Sells in over 100 countries, with Europe its largest region, plus North America and international markets.
rationale: Generics maker selling to pharmacies and payers; low consumer marketing need, so F1 fit is weak.
parent: Spun off from Novartis in 2023

name: Pfizer
desc: US drug maker selling prescription medicines and vaccines, including Prevnar, Eliquis, Ibrance and the Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccine.
markets: Sells to health systems and governments worldwide, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: Zoetis
desc: Animal health company selling medicines, vaccines and diagnostics for pets and livestock to vets and farmers.
markets: Sells in more than 100 countries, with the US its largest market.
rationale: B2B animal health brand; pet medicine marketing exists but F1 fit is weak.
parent: Spun off from Pfizer in 2013

name: Eli Lilly and Company
desc: US drug maker selling diabetes and obesity medicines Mounjaro and Zepbound, cancer, immunology and neuroscience medicines.
markets: Products marketed in about 90 countries, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: Braskem
desc: Brazilian petrochemical company producing polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC and sugarcane-based green polyethylene for plastics makers.
markets: Plants in Brazil, the US, Mexico and Germany; sells resins to converters across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B commodity chemicals producer; green plastics story offers a sustainability angle, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Suzano
desc: Brazilian producer of eucalyptus pulp, paper, paperboard and consumer tissue for manufacturers and retailers.
markets: Exports pulp mainly to China, Europe and North America; owns US paperboard mills; agreed in 2025 to take control of Kimberly-Clark's international tissue business.
rationale: Commodity pulp exporter with mostly B2B customers and little need for consumer brand marketing; weak F1 fit.
parent: Merged with Fibria in 2019

name: Takeda Pharmaceutical
desc: Japanese drug maker selling gastrointestinal, rare-disease, plasma-derived, cancer and neuroscience medicines such as Entyvio.
markets: Operates in around 80 countries; the US is its largest market, followed by Japan and Europe.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Acquired Shire in 2019

name: COFCO Corporation
desc: Chinese state food and agriculture group trading and processing grain, oilseeds and sugar, and selling food brands.
markets: China is the core market; COFCO International trades and sources agricultural commodities across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: State-owned agribusiness with limited marketing need abroad; F1 Shanghai offers some domestic consumer exposure, but fit is weak.
parent: State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (China)

name: UPM-Kymmene
desc: Finnish forest industry group producing pulp, paper, self-adhesive labels, plywood, renewable fuels and energy.
markets: Production mainly in Finland, Uruguay and Germany; sells to customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: B2B materials group; renewable fuels and biomaterials could fit F1 sustainability goals, but brand marketing need is low.

name: Fresenius Medical Care
desc: German provider of kidney dialysis services through outpatient clinics and maker of dialysis machines and dialysers.
markets: About 4,000 dialysis clinics worldwide, with North America its largest market, plus Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B and patient-care business funded largely by regulated reimbursement, with little consumer marketing; weak F1 fit.
parent: Converted to a stock corporation in 2023, ending consolidation by Fresenius SE

name: Amgen
desc: US biotechnology company selling biologic medicines such as Prolia, Repatha, Enbrel and Tezspire, plus biosimilars.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Acquired Horizon Therapeutics in 2023

name: Alltech
desc: US agricultural company making animal feed supplements, yeast products and crop nutrition, with brewing and distilling businesses.
markets: Operations and customers in over 100 countries across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Family-owned B2B agri brand with a record of event sponsorship (World Equestrian Games); F1 hospitality possible, but fit is modest.

name: GSK plc
desc: British drug and vaccine maker selling vaccines such as Shingrix, HIV medicines through ViiV Healthcare, and specialty medicines.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US and Europe as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.
parent: Renamed GSK plc from GlaxoSmithKline in 2022; demerged Haleon in 2022

name: Roche
desc: Swiss healthcare group developing and selling prescription medicines and diagnostic instruments and tests, including Genentech and Chugai.
markets: Sells to hospitals, labs and health systems worldwide, with the US, Europe and Japan as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: Biogen
desc: US biotechnology company selling medicines for multiple sclerosis, spinal muscular atrophy and Alzheimer's disease, such as Spinraza.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US and Europe as major markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: Quintiles
desc: Former contract research organisation that ran clinical trials for drug makers; its business now forms part of IQVIA.
markets: No longer operates separately; its business continues within IQVIA, which serves clients in over 100 countries.
rationale: Brand no longer exists after the merger into IQVIA; no F1 fit for this name.
changed: Merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form QuintilesIMS, renamed IQVIA in 2017

name: Agilent Technologies
desc: Supplier of laboratory instruments such as chromatographs and mass spectrometers, software, consumables and services.
markets: Sells to pharma, chemical, food, environmental and academic labs across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B lab equipment maker with no consumer brand; F1 fit limited to client hospitality.
parent: Spun off from Hewlett-Packard in 1999

name: UCB
desc: Belgian biopharmaceutical company selling medicines for epilepsy and immune diseases, including Keppra, Briviact, Cimzia and Bimzelx.
markets: Sells to health systems worldwide, with the US and Europe as main markets.
rationale: Global pharma selling to health systems and doctors, with heavily regulated consumer promotion; F1 value mainly corporate hospitality and employer branding.

name: Henry Schein
desc: Distributor of dental, medical and practice-management products, equipment and software to dentists, doctors and clinics.
markets: Operations in 33 countries and territories across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: B2B distributor serving dental and medical practices; F1 hospitality could aid customer relations, but brand fit is weak.

name: Zimmer Biomet
desc: US maker of orthopaedic implants for knees, hips and shoulders, surgical instruments and the ROSA surgical robot.
markets: Sells to hospitals and surgeons in more than 100 countries, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Medical device maker selling to hospitals and clinicians; low consumer marketing need, so F1 value is mainly B2B hospitality.

name: ASSA ABLOY
desc: Swedish maker of locks, doors, access control, identity systems and entrance automation under brands such as Yale and HID.
markets: Operations in over 70 countries, with North America and Europe the largest markets, plus Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Security and access technology leader with consumer brand Yale; F1 offers B2B hospitality and a technology showcase, fit moderate.

name: NEC Corporation
desc: Japanese technology group providing IT services, network equipment, biometrics and face recognition, and defence and space systems.
markets: Governments, telecom carriers and enterprises in Japan and worldwide across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: B2B technology supplier with a history of sports sponsorship; F1 offers a biometrics and AI showcase and client hospitality.

name: The Clorox Company
desc: US maker of household and consumer products under Clorox, Brita, Glad, Kingsford, Hidden Valley, Burt's Bees and Pine-Sol brands.
markets: Mainly the United States, with smaller sales in Canada and other international markets.
rationale: US household brands seeking mass reach; F1's growing US audience offers some fit, but marketing is mostly domestic.

name: Alcon
desc: Eye care company making cataract and eye surgery equipment, intraocular lenses, contact lenses and eye drops.
markets: Sells in more than 140 countries to surgeons, optometrists and consumers; main operating base in Fort Worth, Texas.
rationale: Eye care brand with consumer contact lens lines; vision and precision themes could suit F1, but fit is moderate.
parent: Spun off from Novartis in 2019

name: Boston Scientific
desc: US maker of medical devices for cardiology, electrophysiology, urology, endoscopy and neuromodulation, such as the Watchman implant.
markets: Sells to hospitals and clinicians in about 100 countries, with the US its largest market.
rationale: Medical device maker selling to hospitals and clinicians; low consumer marketing need, so F1 value is mainly B2B hospitality.

name: Bausch + Lomb
desc: Eye health company making contact lenses, lens care solutions, eye drops, surgical equipment and prescription eye medicines.
markets: Sells in about 100 countries to consumers, eye doctors and hospitals.
rationale: Consumer eye care brand; vision theme could support F1 activation, though fit is moderate and parent is indebted.
parent: Bausch Health Companies

name: Linde
desc: Industrial gases company supplying oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, argon and specialty gases, plus gas plant engineering.
markets: Customers in healthcare, chemicals, energy, electronics and manufacturing in over 100 countries.
rationale: B2B industrial supplier; hydrogen and engineering story could suit technology messaging, but consumer brand value is low.
parent: Formed by merger of Linde AG and Praxair in 2018

name: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company)
desc: US medical technology company making syringes, needles, catheters, infusion systems and surgical products for hospitals and clinics.
markets: Sells to hospitals, labs and clinics worldwide across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Medical device maker selling to hospitals and clinicians; low consumer marketing need, so F1 value is mainly B2B hospitality.
parent: Agreed in 2025 to combine its Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business with Waters

name: Fresenius
desc: German healthcare group selling injectable drugs, clinical nutrition and biosimilars through Kabi and running Helios hospitals.
markets: Helios hospitals in Germany and Spain; Fresenius Kabi sells in over 100 countries.
rationale: Mainly B2B and hospital operator in Germany and Spain; weak F1 fit beyond corporate hospitality.
parent: Deconsolidated Fresenius Medical Care in 2023 and keeps a minority stake

name: Hims & Hers Health
desc: Telehealth company selling prescription and over-the-counter treatments for hair loss, sexual health, weight loss and skin care by subscription.
markets: Mainly US customers; expanded into the UK and Europe by acquiring Zava in 2025.
rationale: Heavy advertiser targeting young men in the US; F1's growing US male audience gives a clear fit.
parent: Acquired European telehealth company Zava in 2025

name: Solventum
desc: Healthcare company selling wound care, surgical and infection prevention products, dental products and health information software.
markets: Sells to hospitals, clinicians and dentists worldwide across the Americas, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Medical device maker selling to hospitals and clinicians; low consumer marketing need, so F1 value is mainly B2B hospitality.
parent: Spun off from 3M in 2024; sold purification and filtration business to Thermo Fisher in 2025

name: Flo Health
desc: Digital health company operating the Flo app for period and ovulation tracking, pregnancy and women's health, earning from subscriptions.
markets: Users worldwide, with the US and Europe as main subscription markets.
rationale: Consumer app for women; F1's growing female audience gives some fit, but budget is limited.

name: ResMed
desc: Maker of CPAP machines, masks and connected devices for sleep apnea and respiratory conditions, plus out-of-hospital care software.
markets: Sells in about 140 countries, with the US its largest market, plus Europe, Japan and Australia.
rationale: Sleep health brand with patient-facing products; recovery and sleep themes offer some F1 angle, but fit is moderate.

name: Demant
desc: Danish hearing healthcare group making Oticon hearing aids and diagnostic equipment and running hearing clinics.
markets: Sells in over 130 countries, with Europe and North America the largest markets, plus Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Hearing care brand selling to audiologists and older consumers; weak F1 fit.
parent: Sold its hearing implants business to Cochlear in 2024

name: Nutrien
desc: Canadian fertiliser producer of potash, nitrogen and phosphate, running farm retail stores selling crop inputs and services.
markets: Production in Canada and the US; retail stores across North America, South America and Australia.
rationale: Commodity B2B producer selling to farmers; weak F1 fit beyond corporate hospitality.
parent: Formed by merger of Agrium and PotashCorp in 2018
